searchDocs.title: Plugin vs. Animation Module​
searchDocs.content: The RoUI3 plugin is what you actually use to create your animations. This is where you edit keyframes, easing styles, directions, etc. and put together everything. When you're done you'll export your animation.  This is where the RoUI3 animation module comes into play. It is what you use to actually play your animations.

searchDocs.title: Installation​
searchDocs.content: The recommended method of installation is by purchasing RoUI3 directly from the Roblox Creator Store. This will keep you up to date with the plugin and the module (as long as you download the module using the plugin). It also supports the development of RoUI3.

searchDocs.title: 1. Downloading the module​
searchDocs.content: The RoUI3 plugin comes with a download button directly within the plugin itself that fetches the latest version of the module. This will place it into ReplicatedStorage.

searchDocs.title: 2. Creating an animation​
searchDocs.content: local RoUI3 = require(script.RoUI3) -- This is the RoUI3 animation module local myAnimationModule = script.myAnimation -- This is the ModuleScript exported by the RoUI3 plugin local myAnimation = RoUI3.new(myAnimationModule) -- Create a new animation

searchDocs.title: 3. Setting a target​
searchDocs.content: RoUI3 has no way to know where you want to actually use this animation. This is why we need to directly set a target.  myAnimation:SetTarget(script.Parent) -- Assuming the parent is the ScreenGui we animated in RoUI3

searchDocs.title: 4. Playing the animation​
searchDocs.content: With the target set we are ready to play the animation!  myAnimation:Play()   As you can see it's very easy to play RoUI3 animations but there is so much more that can be done.

searchDocs.title: Transforming Keyframes​
searchDocs.content: RoUI3's animation module allows you to dynamically map keyframe values at runtime. This is an extremely powerful feature that, when combined with other tools like animation templates, can make your animations super flexible.  Let's look at the grow animation from earlier. We know that it acts as a template and is reusable on other instances and that the animation itself just grows a GuiObject by 5 pixels in both the X and Y offset. If we want to make a hover animation where the object grows when you hover and then shrinks when you leave you would normally have to go back into the RoUI3 plugin and make a whole new animation. This is tedious and annoying but what if we could just use our existing grow animation? With a keyframe transformer that's exactly what you can do.  We're going to create a brand new shrink animation from our existing grow animation module. We set the targets like we normally would but now here is where things change a little.  local growAnimation = RoUI3.new(growAnimationModule) local shrinkAnimation = RoUI3.new(growAnimationModule) growAnimation:SetTarget(screenGui.Frame) shrinkAnimation:SetTarget(screenGui.Frame)   Remember how our grow animation grows a GuiObject by 5 pixels? Our keyframe transfomer here just takes those 5 pixels and makes them negative and returns that newly calculated change. Now our grow animation adds 5 pixels and our shrink animation subtracts 5 pixels. The transformer is called when keyframe values are calculated which is done when the animation is preloaded.  shrinkAnimation:UseKeyframeTransformer(function(delta: UDim2) return UDim2.new(0, -delta.X.Offset, 0, -delta.Y.Offset) end)   Below we finally just bind our grow and shrink events to create a clean hover growing & shrinking effect.  shrinkAnimation:PreloadAnimation() growAnimation:BindToEvent('MouseEnter', screenGui.Frame) shrinkAnimation:BindToEvent('MouseLeave', screenGui.Frame)   If you don't manually call :PreloadAnimation() then RoUI3 will call it whenever you attempt to play an animation with :Play(). It's worth noting that if you are transforming keyframes in any way with a template animation you should call :PreloadAnimation() when the properties of the instance are exactly as you want them to start out as.

searchDocs.title: __version__​
searchDocs.content: This item is read only and cannot be modified. Read Only </> RoUI3.__version__: string

searchDocs.title: new​
searchDocs.content: </> RoUI3.new(module: ModuleScript ) → RoUI3Animation Creates a new RoUI3 animation object from an exported RoUI3 animation module script.

searchDocs.title: UseKeyframeTransformer​
searchDocs.content: </> RoUI3Animation:UseKeyframeTransformer(transformer: RoUI3KeyframeTransformer) → () Sets a keyframe transformer to use that alters keyframe values when they are generated via :PreloadAnimation(). As a result you must set the transformer before any preloading is done or the keyframe's values will never be properly mapped.

searchDocs.title: PreloadAnimation​
searchDocs.content: </> RoUI3Animation:PreloadAnimation() → () Preloads an animation by internally generating it's tracks, keyframe values, and tweens.

searchDocs.title: WithOptions​
searchDocs.content: </> RoUI3Animation:WithOptions(options: RoUI3AnimationOptions) → RoUI3Animation Sets the options to use when the animation is played and returns the updated animation.

searchDocs.title: BindToEvent​
searchDocs.content: </> RoUI3Animation:BindToEvent( event: string, trigger: Instance , callback: (() → ())? ) → () → () Binds an event of a trigger instance to play an animation. Can pass an optional callback to be called when the event is triggered. If you do pass this paremeter you must :Play() the animation yourself. Returns a function that can be used to clean up the event connection.

searchDocs.title: Completed​
searchDocs.content: </> RoUI3Animation:Completed(callback: () → ()) → () Sets a callback to be called when the animation completes playing.

searchDocs.title: MakeMarker​
searchDocs.content: </> RoUI3Animation:MakeMarker( id: string, at: number, callback: () → () ) → () Makes a marker that has its callback executed when the given time is reached.

searchDocs.title: RemoveMarker​
searchDocs.content: </> RoUI3Animation:RemoveMarker(id: string) → () Removes a marker from the given id.

searchDocs.title: SetTarget​
searchDocs.content: </> RoUI3Animation:SetTarget(target: Instance ) → () Sets a target that the animation will execute upon when played. For standard animations your target should be the ScreenGui you edited when creating your animation with the RoUI3 plugin. Warning: If your animation is a template animation this method will replace all other targets.

searchDocs.title: AddTarget​
searchDocs.content: Template Animation Only </> RoUI3Animation:AddTarget(target: Instance ) → () Adds a target that the animation will execute upon when played. Can only be used in template animations.

searchDocs.title: Play​
searchDocs.content: </> RoUI3Animation:Play() → () Plays an animation.

searchDocs.title: Pause​
searchDocs.content: </> RoUI3Animation:Pause() → () Pauses an animation.

searchDocs.title: Resume​
searchDocs.content: </> RoUI3Animation:Resume() → () Resumes a paused animation.

searchDocs.title: IsPaused​
searchDocs.content: </> RoUI3Animation:IsPaused() → boolean Returns if an animation is paused.

searchDocs.title: Wait​
searchDocs.content: This is a yielding function. When called, it will pause the Lua thread that called the function until a result is ready to be returned, without interrupting other scripts. Yields </> RoUI3Animation:Wait() → () Yields the current thread until a playing animation concludes.

searchDocs.title: Cancel​
searchDocs.content: </> RoUI3Animation:Cancel() → () Cancels an animation.

searchDocs.title: Pause​
searchDocs.content: </> RoUI3Animation:Pause() → () Finishes an animation by jumping to the value of the last keyframe of every track.

searchDocs.title: ResetTargets​
searchDocs.content: </> RoUI3Animation:ResetTargets() → () Resets all targets to their initial states before the animation played. The initial state used is cached whenever :PreloadAnimation() is called.

searchDocs.title: Reset​
searchDocs.content: </> RoUI3Animation:Reset() → () Resets almost the entire animation's state so it can be reused. The following is preserved when this method is called: Targets Animation Options Set Keyframe Transformer Bound Events Completed Callback

searchDocs.title: Destroy​
searchDocs.content: </> RoUI3Animation:Destroy() → () Destroys an animation & completely cleans it up.
